mappings.note: Asks what platelets do for the body - initiate clotting, limit blood loss. Role outcome; no structural feature of the tissue is required.
The relationship asked for is functional: tendons attach skeletal muscle to bone and pass on the contractile force. No injury or activity framing, so C-5.3-LO-2 is not cited.
The structural signature of cardiac fibres (cylindrical, branched, uninucleate, faintly striated) is exactly what separates cardiac from striated and smooth muscle in LO-1.
Defines the axon by its form (long thin fibre from the cell body) and the job that form does (carrying impulses onward) - structure related to function.

Names the joint type behind a movement range - joint-types clause of LO-1. Deliberately narrower than the athlete warm-up MCQ, which adds C-5.3-LO-2 because of its activity framing; this stem has none.
Locating a named joint type in the body is part of knowing the joint types LO-1 lists. Nothing about movement quality or tissue condition is asked.
Straight statement of what the rib cage does for the organism - shielding heart and lungs. Role outcome.

The joint type is given in the stem, so no classification is scored; what is scored is the consequence of losing its protective role. Split from the skull assertion-reason item, which does require the joint type to be judged (LO-1).

Totipotency demonstrated in culture is the frontier-biology content of this chapter (C7.1); C8.2 second because what is asked is the experimental condition - the nutrient medium and hormones - that the demonstration depends on.
Terminology recall for totipotency. C7.1 is the only competency in the frame that houses regenerative-biology content; LO-5, its single outcome, is about muscular injury and cannot take it.

Poor fit, recorded as such. The question is pure history of science (who, and in what year), and the frame has no history-of-science outcome except C6.1, which is specifically about contributions from India - Steward is neither Indian nor current. C7.1 is cited only because the underlying concept is the frontier content.
Crown gall is uncontrolled division producing tumour swellings, i.e. what happens when dividing tissue escapes its normal role in the plant. Fit is loose; the frame has no outcome for plant disease.

Agrobacterium as a gene-transfer tool is a present-day application well beyond the textbook tissue content, which is what C7.1 exists for. Split from the previous item, which stays on the plant biology of the disease itself.
Names the tissue from what it does at a joint (cushioning, shock absorption). Role outcome; the cartilage clause of C-5.3-LO-2 is not triggered because no fitness or activity context is present.
The error to be corrected is a muscle-type misattribution on both counts, voluntary control and the action performed - the striated/smooth/cardiac discrimination in LO-1.

Plant-versus-animal tissue difference (LO-1) argued from what each way of life demands of its tissues - support against movement - hence the role outcome second. Split from the dead-tissue item below, which argues from what the tissues are made of.
Division of labour through tissue formation in a multicellular body is the level-of-organisation outcome. No particular tissue's structure or role is scored, only the principle.

The stem asks for justification from structural requirements, so the argument runs from dead, lignified, low-maintenance cells to mechanical strength (C-4.2-LO-2); LO-1 second for the plant/animal contrast the claim rests on.

The scored explanation is what apical meristem does - continuous division giving increase in length. The labelled-diagram half has no home in this frame: C-8.2-LO-2 covers figures that represent data, and an anatomical location diagram is not that.

The clearest C3.2 item in the chapter: it asks for similarities and differences in the life process of nutrition, photosynthesis against ingestion, which is that competency verbatim. LO-1 second for the consequent plant/animal tissue difference. Not C4.1 - no classification into kingdoms is asked.
First half is structure-to-function (why the absence of vacuoles suits division); second half is differentiation, the meristematic-to-permanent transition that sits under LO-1. Two halves, two codes.

The cut-root-tip experiment named by LO-6. Kept to one code as the third member of that family: the part-1 item adds C8.2 because it asks for the procedure to be sequenced, the part-2 item adds C-8.2-LO-2 because it supplies a data table, and this one supplies neither - only the outcome and the tissue behind it.
The scored question is why the corners are thickened and what that buys the plant - pectin deposition giving strength with flexibility. The drawing half is not covered by any outcome in this frame.

One of the few items that genuinely earns three codes: it names the pair to be told apart (LO-1) and then demands the structural differences (C-4.2-LO-2) and the functional ones (C-4.2-LO-3) separately.
Fresh versus dry twig is one tissue in two states, not two tissues, so nothing is being differentiated in the LO-1 sense; what is scored is why living pectin-thickened walls bend and dried ones snap.
